_comment: CLAUDE.md size ratchet CEILING (W1-T503, MASTER-PLAN 8A). capBytes is the only figure declared here -- the actual byte size is measured fresh from the committed CLAUDE.md by `node scripts/claude-md-budget-ratchet.mjs` on every run (W1-T1234: a stored measured figure went stale on every edit to CLAUDE.md and reddened the gate for a reason no PR caused). capBytes carries deliberate headroom over the file's typical size, which is a change from the zero-headroom shape this baseline held until 2026-08-22 -- see bumpRationale for the current raise and priorBumpRationale for the one that retired zero-headroom. IT IS NO LONGER A ROUND BOUNDARY: 65536 (64 KiB) was chosen for legibility on 2026-08-22 and the 2026-08-28 raise traded that legibility for a stated +2000 increment, so do not 'restore' a power of two by rounding this figure in either direction. The ceiling still fails closed and still only ever ratchets UP by a reviewed bump that says why growth is right; never lower it to make a red PR pass, and never raise it to paper over an unreviewed dump of new rules.
bumpRationale: RE-DERIVED 44000 -> 17000 by W1-T3341 on 2026-09-11, the instrument-only PR Standing rule 25 requires. W1-T3323 moved 41595 bytes of rule BODIES out of CLAUDE.md into doctrine/ and left the cap at 44000 against a 15501-byte file: 284% of the file, admitting roughly 150 new rules before refusing. That is not a ratchet, and the gate spent that whole window gating nothing. THE UNIT OF GROWTH CHANGED, WHICH IS WHY THE OLD ARITHMETIC CANNOT BE SCALED DOWN. A new rule used to cost this file its whole body -- 610 bytes on the MEASURED average of 56 rules over 34198. It now costs a headline plus a pointer. RE-MEASURED ON THE LIVE INDEX (which the shard's falsifier demanded rather than reusing its own estimate, and the re-measurement CORRECTED it): 7301 bytes of headlines over 56 rules is 130.4 each, and the 56 `-> doctrine/<section>/<rule>.md` pointers are 5290 bytes -- 94.5 each, not the ~55 the filing guessed. So a rule costs 224.8 bytes, and 17000 leaves 1499 bytes = 6.7 RULES of headroom, about 10.9 days once W1-T2507's measured 374 bytes/day is repriced from 610-byte rules to 224.8-byte ones (~138 bytes/day). The filing claimed eight rules and thirteen days; the honest figures are 6.7 and 10.9, and the cap is kept at the reviewed 17000 rather than nudged upward to make the round number come out -- fitting a bound to a narrative is how a ceiling stops meaning anything. FOLDING NOW MEANS SHORTENING A HEADLINE, not deleting a measurement: the body is retrieved, never injected, so prose in doctrine/ costs an interactive session nothing and cutting it buys nothing. That is also why doctrine/ has no ceiling of its own -- learnings/*.yaml is budgeted because it is INJECTED, and this store is not. NEVER raise this back toward 44000 to make a red PR pass: at 224.8 bytes a rule that is 126 rules of headroom, which retires the gate rather than loosening it.
priorBumpRationale: LOWERED 67536 -> 44000 by W1-T2507 on 2026-08-31, THE FIRST TIME THIS RATCHET HAS EVER MOVED DOWN. The two prior entries below raised the cap twice because the file itself kept growing and folding it further kept costing more than it saved -- W1-T2507 changed the OTHER variable: it moved content OUT of CLAUDE.md rather than compressing what stayed. Three moves, none of them a rule deletion: (1) 19 bullets that each named a concrete repo path became learnings/architecture.yaml entries whose files: glob matches exactly that path, so the fact now reaches the task that governs it and no other -- the destination this repo already built and measured (W1-T33/W1-T38). Three MORE bullets were drafted for the same move and REVERTED: existing regression tests (test/docs-claims.test.ts, test/rule-citations-match-their-rule.test.ts, test/ci-gate-reaggregate.test.ts, test/fleet-heartbeat-image-sha.test.ts) pin their exact prose inside CLAUDE.md itself, proving those particular facts are read by every task author regardless of files: -- not just editors of the one file they happen to name -- so migrating them would have LOST reach rather than preserved it; they stayed. (2) the 'Operating this host' section -- rules about the daemon's own mac-mini host (shared node_modules, launchd, the worktree-reaping directory) that a containerised worker can never act on -- moved to docs/operator-guide.md, the document its actual reader (a human operating that host) already consults; ONE bullet from that section (the mount-vs-image-rebuild boundary) came back for the same reason as above -- a worker editing deploy/ needs it, proven by test/fleet-heartbeat-image-sha.test.ts. (3) the five dated 'Lessons from <date>' sections, an append-only log the file's own maintenance rule forbids, folded into the topical sections they belong to, with letter sequences renumbered so no gap is left. The file measures 42606 bytes after all moves (vs 67535 before, one byte under the old cap), and 44000 restores deliberate headroom -- about 1400 bytes -- so the ratchet keeps its designed job of forcing a fold-or-migrate decision on the NEXT addition rather than sitting so far under cap that growth goes unnoticed for weeks. NEVER raise this back toward 67536 to make a red PR pass without first checking whether the growth is itself a bullet that names a concrete path or belongs in a dated section -- those have a cheaper move than raising the cap, PROVIDED no existing test pins that bullet's prose inside CLAUDE.md itself (grep test/*.test.ts for the bullet's distinctive phrase before moving it). See learnings/architecture.yaml's newest entries (`migrated from CLAUDE.md`, W1-T2507) and docs/operator-guide.md's new 'Operating this host' section for the migrated content itself. CORRECTION (W1-T2759): every figure here prices the INTERACTIVE lane. A dispatched worker never loads CLAUDE.md at all -- spawnWorker passes settingSources: [], which the SDK documents as isolation mode requiring 'project' to load CLAUDE.md files.
foldDebtRationale: RE-DERIVED 48000 -> 18400 by W1-T3341 on 2026-09-11, as the W1-T3323 entry it replaces required: carrying 48000 forward left a debt allowance 3x the whole file. THE MEANING IS UNCHANGED (operator ruling 2026-09-10: a gate repairs, routes or closes; a stop is for harm, not incompleteness): capBytes is where the gate starts FILING a fold follow-up and lets the change land, and THIS is where it really refuses. It stays a debt allowance, not a second cap, because 'we can always take on some tech debt' is only true while the debt is collected -- 45 parked verify:human shards, the oldest seven weeks (W1-T3206), are what an uncollected queue looks like. THE ARITHMETIC, ON THE RE-MEASURED UNIT: a rule adds 224.8 bytes to this file, so 18400 admits 2899 bytes = 12.9 rules past the file's current size, of which 6.7 are under the cap and about SIX are the unfolded-debt window -- close to the seven the old 4000-byte allowance bought at 610 bytes a rule, which is the property being preserved. ABSENT, ROUTING IS DISABLED and the gate behaves as it did before W1-T3320: a missing bound must never read as an infinite one.
